subject: Re: Order Form amendment — subcontractor scope & DPA onboarding timeline
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice@brightsky.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@brightsky.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form amendment — subcontractor scope update

Hi Marissa,

Quick note from procurement — we received an internal change request: one of our regional data processors (EdgeStream Services) will be added as a downstream subcontractor to the order form for the event-analytics integration. We need Redwood to confirm two things before we can sign the amended order form:

1) Confirmation that EdgeStream will be bound by the same DPA terms (Schedule A) or an equivalent flow-down, and whether Redwood will issue a subprocessor notice.
2) A short timeline for DPA onboarding (we need evidence within 10 business days for our audit).

I've attached the updated order form (BrightSky_OrderForm_v2.pdf) and a marked-up Schedule A that shows our preferred additions. Can you confirm who on your side will handle the subprocessor notification and whether the redlines are acceptable?

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Procurement Manager
BrightSky Analytics

[Attachment: BrightSky_OrderForm_v2.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@brightsky.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Aug 2025 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form amendment — subcontractor scope update

Alice — thanks for the heads up and the files. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Priya (privacy/compliance).

High level: Redwood intends to issue a subprocessor notice to BrightSky and to use a standard flow-down where feasible. We need to validate EdgeStream's technical controls against Schedule A and confirm whether they accept our preferred redline language (we often require the subproc to accept identical DPA obligations rather than a materially equivalent set).

Can Kimberly confirm whether we can accept BrightSky's marked changes as-is or if we need targeted counter-redlines? Priya — can your team run a quick control-gap check on EdgeStream (we have their SOC summary from last year) and indicate whether we can provide evidence within 10 business days?

Proposed next steps:
- Kimberly to provide legal guidance on redlines (EOD Fri).
- Priya to review EdgeStream controls and confirm evidence we can supply (by Mon 9/1).
- I will prepare the formal subprocessor notice and draft DocuSign envelope for signature if we land on language.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Aug 2025 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form amendment — subcontractor scope update

Marissa / Priya — quick read-through below. I reviewed BrightSky's marked Schedule A (DPA_Schedule_A_redlines.docx). Notable items:

- BrightSky inserted clause 2.3 (downstream notice & proof) that asks for evidence within 10 business days. Acceptable, but we should negotiate the evidence scope (logs/config snapshots vs. full reports).
- They modified our indemnity carve-out language to broaden it to downstream subcontractor acts. We should push back — propose limiting to gross negligence/willful misconduct by the subprocessor.
- They requested direct flow-down that makes EdgeStream a benefit-holder under Redwood's MSA terms. That could create direct contractual privity issues. Suggest we provide an explicit subproc agreement that binds EdgeStream to key DPA obligations without making them a direct party to the MSA.

Suggested counter-redlines (summary):
1) Accept notice + evidence request but limit evidence to control attestations, SOC summary, and a security questionnaire (we can provide a pre-filled questionnaire).
2) Retain existing indemnity carve-out; if BrightSky insists, accept narrowly limited language tied to proven breach attributable to EdgeStream.
3) Add a clause that requires BrightSky to notify Redwood prior to exercising any contractual remedies against EdgeStream that would affect Redwood operations (protects us operationally).

I can draft the counter-redlines in tracked changes — target EOD today. If BrightSky insists on 10-business-day evidence and refuses control attestation, we can offer a one-time exception for onboarding with mitigations (short-term monitoring + restricted signing).

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: DPA_Schedule_A_redlines.docx]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Sep 2025 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form amendment — subcontractor scope update

Folks — I ran a quick control-gap check against EdgeStream's SOC summary and our standard onboarding checklist. Findings:

- EdgeStream has encryption at rest + in transit, role-based access controls, and a recent penetration test (report redacted).
- Missing: documented retention policy aligned to BrightSky's region-specific retention limits, and evidence of continuous logging to an immutable store.

What we can provide in 10 business days:
- SOC summary + pen test attestation (redacted copies).
- Completed security questionnaire (I will pre-fill and send to EdgeStream).
- Pseudonymization notes and a short design doc describing how EdgeStream isolates BrightSky event data (see evidence_pseudonymization_notes.pdf).

If BrightSky needs immutable-logging proofs, we may need an extra week to coordinate with EdgeStream's ops team. I recommend offering the 10-business-day window for the attestation package we have, and a 7-day extension for low-level operational artifacts.

I will coordinate the evidence collection and share the pre-filled questionnaire by Wed 8/31.

Priya Natarajan
Senior Privacy Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: evidence_pseudonymization_notes.pdf]

From: Alice Chen <alice@brightsky.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@brightsky.ai>, Erik Jansen <erik.j@legalco.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Aug 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form amendment — subcontractor scope update

Marissa / Kimberly / Priya — thanks for the quick reviews and the plan. A couple of clarifications from our side before we proceed to DocuSign: 

- Our audit team will accept SOC summary + security questionnaire for initial onboarding. The immutable-logging artifacts are a lower priority but we will want them within 30 days of go-live.
- On indemnity: BrightSky cannot accept carve-outs that leave us without a remedy for a subproc-caused data exposure. We can be flexible on wording (narrowed to proven fault) but need operational recourse.
- Please include the subprocessor notice template in your counter-redlines so our legal team can review it alongside the tracked changes.

If we can get the counter-redlines and the subproc notice template today, our legal team will triage and aim to sign the order form by next week. We'll wait for the DocuSign link.

Best,
Alice
Procurement Manager, BrightSky Analytics
